newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi wins confidence test, doubts linger.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi wins confidence test, doubts linger.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi survived his second parliamentary confidence vote within three days on Saturday and warned his bickering coalition that if it did not stay united, Italy would be ruined.

President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro ordered the do-or-die confidence votes in the upper and lower houses of parliament after Prodi's hard-left ally refused to tow the government line on a security mission for Albania.
The multinational operation, which is being led by Italy and is due to swing into action next week, was only saved with the help of the centre-right opposition.

But the hard-left Communist Refoundation, which secures Prodi's majority in the lower house of parliament and has a been a persistent source of bother to the prime minister, returned to the coalition fold for the confidence votes.
Prodi won Saturday's motion by 321 votes to 262, but told the house he was no longer prepared to brook dissent from Refoundation.

"We cannot have other wrenches as serious as this one. They will no longer be accepted," Prodi said, adding that the problems faced by Italy as it sought to become a founder member of the single European currency would be hurt by further divisions among government allies.
"The call for coalition unity is not a call for the continuity of this government but for the salvation of the country," Prodi told the assembly.
Prodi came to power last May at the head of a broad based centre-left administration, but has always struggled to live with the hardline Refoundation.

Other coalition partners have threatened to quit the government if Prodi fails to reach a detailed accord with Refoundation over policy and called on the prime minister on Saturday to seek an immediate clarification of future goals.
"This clarification has not finished, it has only just begun and should be about hard facts," Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, head of the small centrist Italian Renewal party, said.
Opposition politicians said Prodi had been badly injured over the split with Refoundation on the Albania mission and said the country was suffering as a result.
"Unfortunately, while the government is being weakened, the problems of the country are only getting worse," said Beppe Pisanu, parliamentary party leader of the centre-right Forza Italia party.

Prodi said he had three main goals ahead of him -- to reinforce his majority and keep it united, to continue overhauling state accounts to ensure Italy is on the first train to the European single currency, and press for constitutional reform, currently under debate in a parliamentary committee.
He added that he also intended to launch an immediate review of the welfare state. "On structural measures, a difficult road lies ahead of us," he said.
